source: make 3d tower defense rng make a map like grow a garden

image_prompt.text: Flat soil beds and planting plots framing both sides of the track where players place their defenders
A narrowing in the garden path where waves bunch up and area damage pays off
The structure at the end of the path standing for the player health pool, dressed as the heart of the garden

layout_placement.text: The mouth of the garden path where each enemy wave enters
The core base at the end of the track carrying the primary health pool

notes: lane-actor-track routes P6: the enemy lane has to be one valid continuous route, generated first and dressed after, so it is never an image-model invention.

Make a map like grow a garden is a reference to another game. It was read as a theme instruction - soil, beds, planting rows - because nothing in the handoff can carry a named reference title, and the preset reference column is internal and must not be echoed back.
RNG here means rolling for towers rather than anything spatial; it does not change the map.

open_questions.ask: When you say a map like Grow a Garden, do you mean the planting-plot look specifically, or just a bright outdoor garden?
One winding path, or several lanes converging on the same base?
What does the RNG roll for - the towers you get to place, or the enemies that show up?

theme: Garden - tilled soil, flower beds, planting rows under bright daylight

answers.ask: When you say a map like Grow a Garden, do you mean the planting-plot look specifically, or just a bright outdoor garden?
answers.answer: Use the planting-plot look specifically: a bright, colorful outdoor garden with neat farm plots and simple cozy props.

answers.ask: One winding path, or several lanes converging on the same base?
answers.answer: Use one winding path to keep the first map small and easy to play.

answers.ask: What does the RNG roll for - the towers you get to place, or the enemies that show up?
answers.answer: The RNG rolls for the towers the player gets to place.
